messages:
morgan: Heads-up — product wants to retire /v1/generate and migrate traffic to /v2 over the next 6 months. We need a compatibility/shim strategy before announcing.
ravi: Agreed. Two main options: full gateway rewrite vs runtime compatibility mode. Gateway is faster to ship but misses some runtime behaviors (streaming framing, kv-cache layout, and alias pinning).
chen: Streaming is the kicker. Rewriting paths/headers at the gateway level doesn't fix chunked SSE framing differences. We saw similar bugs when we migrated the chat endpoint last year.
tess: I'm in favor of a split approach: gateway does param/header normalization and basic mapping; runtime implements a minimal compat flag to preserve legacy kv ordering, alias mapping, and old function-calling payload shapes.
morgan: That matches my thinking. We should also assume many customers use SDKs; SDKs can be patched to auto-upgrade clients. But raw HTTP users need server-side shims for at least 3-6 months.
ravi: Proposal draft:
- Phase A (0-30d): Gateway normalization only. Map deprecated params -> new params, set X-Redwood-Compat:legacy for v1 path detections.
- Phase B (30-90d): Runtime compat flag. When X-Redwood-Compat present, runtime preserves legacy kv ordering and disables select new kernel heuristics for that request.
- Phase C (90-180d): Telemetry review. If stable, start soft enforcement (10% redirects -> 100%).
chen: I'll add E2E tests covering: streaming SSE interleaving, function-calling payloads, and alias->checkpoint mapping behind the gateway+runtime combo.
tess: Telemetry needs: compat_tag source (path|sdk|header), shimed_traffic_pct, shim_error_delta (streaming vs native), p50/p95 latency delta, memory overhead by context-length for compat requests.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary for cluster redwood-serving-2 at 03:15 UTC with env REDWOOD_COMPAT_GATEWAY=true
ravi: One operational note: preserving legacy kv layout increases memory usage for long contexts. Add a memory-aware fallback that shortens kv retention when host memory pressure > threshold.
morgan: Docs & SDK plan: release SDK patch that defaults to v2 behavior but sets X-Redwood-Compat for a grace period. Publish migration guide with REST and streaming snippets and a small adapter library for streaming callback differences.
chen: Quick nginx test snippet I used while prototyping:
```
local uri = ngx.var.request_uri
if uri:find("/v1/generate") then
  ngx.req.set_uri(uri:gsub("/v1/","/v2/"), false)
  ngx.req.set_header("X-Redwood-Compat","legacy")
end
```
tess: Rollout checklist additions:
- alias mapping table (old alias -> pinned checkpoint id)
- SDK adapter and release notes
- telemetry dashboard + alert for shim error spike
- kill-switch via feature-flag in the gateway
morgan: Action items and owners:
- chen: alias mapping table + E2E tests (due EOW)
- ravi: runtime compat flag design + memory fallback (PR next Tue)
- tess: telemetry dashboard + rollout metrics (dash draft by Wed)
- docs: migration guide + SDK notes (draft by EOW)
- ops: schedule canary and ensure kill-switch (ops-bot queued)
morgan: We'll do a short sync after the PRs land to lock windows. Thanks everyone.
ops-bot: note: canary scheduled; use feature flag REDWOOD_COMPAT_GATEWAY; contact @oncall if issues.
